title: TQL: Scaling Q-Functions with Transformers by Preventing Attention Collapse
claim: Naively scaling models degrades performance because internal attention collapses; our method preserves attention and keeps improving as capacity grows.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, shared orange highlight for ours against gray baselines
description: Two line plots side by side, with the method in orange and the baselines in gray. The left panel plots relative improvement (%) against critic model size (0.4M to 26M). The orange line climbs steadily and is labeled +18%, +29% and +43%. Four gray baselines (floq, FQL, PAC, Transformer w/o TQL) stay flat or fall below a dashed zero line. An inset at top left shows growing circles for critic size and cartoon agents for performance. The right panel plots attention entropy against training steps. The gray transformer curve drops sharply and stays low, annotated 'Attention Collapse'. The orange curve holds near 3.2, annotated 'Stable Attention'. Legends sit below each plot. Orange titles in monospace type draw the eye first.
caption: TQL unlocks scaling of value functions in RL by preventing attention collapse. Left: Scaling results of TQL compared with prior approaches with different generative model backbones. The results are reported as relative improvement over the smallest model size, averaged across seeds and all 25 tasks in our evaluation suite. TQL increases in performance as network size increases, while prior approaches are not able to effectively use the extra capacity and drop in performance. Right: Attention entropy with and without TQL, averaged across 25 tasks. TQL scales effectively by preventing attention collapse that occurs with scaling up the transformer architecture for value function training.
abstract: Despite scale driving substantial recent advancements in machine learning, reinforcement learning (RL) methods still primarily use small value functions. Naively scaling value functions -- including with a transformer architecture, which is known to be highly scalable -- often results in learning instability and worse performance. In this work, we ask what prevents transformers from scaling effectively for value functions? Through empirical analysis, we identify the critical failure mode in this scaling: attention scores collapse as capacity increases. Our key insight is that we can effectively prevent this collapse and stabilize training by controlling the entropy of the attention scores, thereby enabling the use of larger models. To this end, we propose Transformer Q-Learning (TQL), a method that unlocks the scaling potential of transformers in learning value functions in RL. Our approach yields up to a 43% improvement in performance when scaling from the smallest to the largest network sizes, while prior methods suffer from performance degradation.
